story_type: crewed capsule reentry seen from the pilot's window, plasma at Mach 35, crew recovered
hook: Four astronauts sat behind this window as it turned to fire.
narration: Four astronauts sat behind this window as it turned to fire.
This is Artemis two, coming home from a nearly ten day trip around the Moon and back.
Before re-entry, the capsule turned so its heat shield faced the atmosphere.
The shield takes the heat on the outside, so the people inside can survive it.
They hit the air at thirty five times the speed of sound.
Plasma built up around the capsule, and for about six minutes, the radio went silent.
Streaks of glowing light shot past the glass.
outcome: Orion splashed down off San Diego, and the whole crew was brought safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha.
title: Artemis II crew window as it hits Mach 35
description:
On April 10, 2026, NASA's Artemis II Orion spacecraft re-entered Earth's atmosphere at about 35 times the speed of sound, carrying astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen home from their trip around the Moon. A camera at the pilot's forward window recorded the plasma. The crew splashed down off San Diego.
